weeks.title: Essential Khaleeji Greetings & Social Honorifics
weeks.objective: Master conversational Gulf Arabic greetings, appropriate honorifics, and everyday courteous responses.

slides.title: The Universal Greeting: Salam Alaykum
slides.body: In the UAE and the broader Arab world, conversations begin with warmth and respectful greetings before any business is discussed. The universal greeting 'As-salamu alaykum' translates to 'Peace be upon you', and the reciprocal response is 'Wa alaykum as-salam'.
bullets: As-salamu alaykum -> Response: Wa alaykum as-salam (And upon you be peace)
Marhaban -> Response: Marhaban bik / Ahlan wa sahlan (Welcome)
Sabah al-khayr -> Response: Sabah an-noor (Good morning / Morning of light)
Masa' al-khayr -> Response: Masa' an-noor (Good evening / Evening of light)
slides.takeaway: Using local Khaleeji expressions like 'Sh-halak' and 'Mashkoor' creates immediate goodwill with Emirati citizens.

slides.title: Honorifics & Respectful Address
slides.body: Addressing people correctly demonstrates cultural awareness. In Dubai, leaders and citizens hold traditional titles that reflect royal lineage, public service, or religious pilgrimages.
bullets: Sheikh (m) / Sheikha (f): Member of a ruling family, or an esteemed religious/tribal leader
Sayyid (m) / Sayyida (f): Formal address for 'Mr.' or 'Mrs.' in professional correspondence
Abu [Eldest Son's Name]: Friendly, highly respectful teknonym (e.g. Abu Rashid = Father of Rashid)
Um [Eldest Son's Name]: Respectful teknonym for mothers
slides.codeSnippet:
Common Courtesies:
Phrase             | Pronunciation   | When to Use
Inshallah          | In-sha-Allah    | 'God willing' (When planning future events)
Alhamdulillah      | Al-ham-du-lillah | 'Praise be to God' (When asked how you are)
Mashallah          | Ma-sha-Allah    | Expressing admiration without envy
Afwan              | Af-wan          | 'You are welcome' / 'Excuse me'
Habibi / Habibti   | Ha-bee-bee      | 'My friend / My dear' (Informal friendly)
slides.takeaway: Honorifics express deep social respect; never address a member of the ruling family without the title 'His/Her Highness Sheikh/Sheikha'.

caseStudy.scenario: An Emirati business partner asks you: 'Sh-halak?' (How are you?). What is the most natural and courteous response?

options.explanation: 'La' means 'No' and walking away is rude.

quiz.question: What Khaleeji word is commonly used in Dubai to warmly say 'Thank you'?
quiz.explanation: 'Mashkoor' (masculine) / 'Mashkoorah' (feminine) is the standard Gulf Arabic expression for thank you.

weeks.title: Dubai Civic & Government Terminology
weeks.objective: Navigate official Dubai public portals, government department acronyms, and essential administrative words.

slides.title: Decoding Dubai Government Entities
slides.body: Interacting with Dubai's government services is remarkably streamlined, but knowing the Arabic terms behind official departments and documents helps you navigate permits, visas, and legal paperwork effortlessly.
bullets: Amer: Government customer service centers handling residency visas, Emirates IDs, and entry permits
Tasheel: Service centers specialized in MOHRE labor contracts and work permits
Tawjeeh: Centers providing labor awareness and guidance for employees and employers
Ejari: Meaning 'My Rent' in Arabic; the DLD lease registration system
slides.codeSnippet:
Essential Civic Vocabulary:
Arabic Term  | Meaning / Institution          | Context
الهوية      | Al-Hawiyyah (Emirates ID)       | Mandatory identity card
الإقامة     | Al-Iqamah (Residency Visa)     | Passport residency stamp/e-visa
بلدية دبي   | Baladiyyat Dubai                | Dubai Municipality
محاكم دبي   | Mahakim Dubai                   | Dubai Courts
شرطة دبي   | Shurtat Dubai                   | Dubai Police
هيئة الطرق  | RTA (Hay'at at-Turuq)           | Roads & Transport Authority
slides.takeaway: Recognizing administrative Arabic terms saves time when navigating digital portals like Dubai Now and ICP.

slides.title: Official Terminology for Business & Residency
slides.body: When setting up companies, leasing offices, or managing staff, specific Arabic legal concepts appear repeatedly in contracts and official trade license documents.
bullets: Wakala: Power of Attorney (delegating legal authority to a representative)
Daman: Security deposit or financial guarantee
Tashira: Official entry visa
Ghurfat Dubai: Dubai Chamber of Commerce
slides.takeaway: Ensure your commercial contracts contain both verified English and Arabic text, as Arabic remains the official legal language of UAE courts.

weeks.title: Souk Bargaining, Taxis & Restaurant Arabic
weeks.objective: Converse confidently in the Gold and Spice Souks, guide RTA taxi drivers, and order authentic local dishes.

slides.title: The Art of Courteous Souk Bargaining
slides.body: Bargaining in Dubai's traditional souks (Deira Gold Souk, Spice Souk, Textile Souk) is an enjoyable cultural dance, not a confrontation. Polite humor, mutual respect, and Arabic phrases earn lower prices and warm merchant hospitality.
bullets: Kam hadha?: 'How much is this?'
Ghaali ktheer!: 'Too expensive!' (said with a friendly smile)
A'tini aakhir si'r: 'Give me your final/best price'
Kammil: 'Make it a round figure / discount it'
slides.codeSnippet:
Souk Bargaining Dialogue:
Buyer: 'As-salamu alaykum! Kam hadha al-z'afaran?' (How much is this saffron?)
Merchant: '100 Dirhams ya habibi.'
Buyer: 'Mashallah jameel, lakin ghaali ktheer! A'tini aakhir si'r.' (Beautiful, but too expensive! Give me your final price.)
Merchant: 'Lil-tayyibin... 75 Dirhams.' (For good people... 75)
Buyer: 'Khalliha 60 Dirhams wa mashkoor.' (Make it 60 and thank you.)
slides.takeaway: Always maintain a relaxed, respectful demeanor when negotiating in souks; aggressive bargaining is counterproductive.

slides.title: Directional Arabic for Taxis & Daily Commutes
slides.body: While most Dubai taxi drivers speak English, knowing key directional Arabic words ensures smooth navigation through historic neighborhoods and congested routes.
bullets: Yameen: Right | Yasaar: Left | Seedah / Ala Tool: Straight ahead
Hina / Ihna: Here | Hinaak: Over there
Waggif hina, low samaht: 'Stop here, please'
Kammil seedah: 'Continue straight ahead'
slides.codeSnippet:
Daily Navigation Words:
Word          | Meaning
Seedah        | Straight ahead
Yameen        | Right
Yasaar        | Left
Shari'        | Street / Road
Jisr          | Bridge
Dawwar        | Roundabout
Mahattah      | Station (Metro / Petrol)
slides.takeaway: Saying 'Seedah' and 'Waggif hina, low samaht' gets you to your destination with clarity and politeness.

weeks.title: Business Etiquette & Cross-Cultural Sensitivity
weeks.objective: Master professional meetings, Ramadan protocol, public decorum, and building authentic long-term trust in the UAE.

slides.title: Professional Meetings & The Personal Connection
slides.body: In the UAE corporate culture, relationships precede business transactions. Rushing straight into contract terms without inquiring about family, health, and mutual acquaintances is perceived as transactional and impatient.
bullets: Relationship First: The first 15 minutes of a meeting are devoted to hospitality and personal rapport
Patience (Sabr): Decisions frequently involve consensus building among senior partners and family stakeholders
Handshake Etiquette: Do not offer to shake hands with a local woman unless she extends her hand first; otherwise, place your right hand over your heart with a slight nod
slides.codeSnippet:
Business Decorum Best Practices:
1. Stand up when someone enters the room, especially elders or female colleagues
2. Never show the soles of your shoes directly to someone in a meeting
3. Pass business cards, documents, and drinks with your RIGHT hand
4. Dress conservatively and professionally (smart business attire)
5. Respect prayer times (avoid scheduling over noon Dhuhr prayer)
slides.takeaway: Placing your right hand over your heart with a gentle bow is a universally respected sign of courtesy in the UAE.

slides.title: The Holy Month of Ramadan & Public Etiquette
slides.body: Ramadan is the most sacred month in the Islamic calendar, marked by fasting from dawn until sunset, charitable giving (Zakat), and spiritual reflection. Understanding and honoring Ramadan customs reflects profound cultural respect.
bullets: Ramadan Kareem / Ramadan Mubarak: Traditional greeting wishing a generous and blessed month
Iftar: The evening meal breaking the fast at sunset, traditionally starting with dates and water
Suhoor: The pre-dawn meal consumed before beginning the fast
Public Fasting Etiquette: Refrain from eating, drinking, or chewing gum in public outdoor spaces during daylight hours
slides.codeSnippet:
Ramadan Etiquette Summary:
- Greet colleagues with: 'Ramadan Kareem' (May Ramadan be generous)
- Working Hours: Private and public sector working hours are reduced by 2 hours daily
- Iftar Gatherings: Accepting an invitation to an Iftar is an honor and deepens personal bonds
- Modesty: Dress more conservatively in public spaces during the holy month
slides.takeaway: Embracing UAE cultural traditions transforms expatriates from temporary visitors into respected, integrated members of the community.

caseStudy.scenario: You are introduced to an Emirati businesswoman in a professional executive boardroom. What is the correct greeting etiquette regarding physical contact?

options.text: Immediately reach out and grab both of her hands warmly.
options.explanation: Impolite and violates personal space and cultural boundaries.

options.text: Wait to see if she extends her hand first. If she does not, place your right hand over your heart with a respectful nod and warm greeting.
options.explanation: This is the universally accepted and culturally refined etiquette in the UAE.

options.text: Turn your back and ignore her entirely.

quiz.question: What is the evening meal called that breaks the daily fast at sunset during Ramadan?
